title: Within Range
statement:
Check whether a number lies inside a range, counting both ends of the range.

The input is one line with three integers separated by spaces: `x`, then `lo`, then `hi`. You can assume `lo <= hi`. Any of them can be negative. Print `true` when `lo <= x` and `x <= hi`, and `false` otherwise. A value equal to `lo` or `hi` counts as inside.

Input:

```text
5 1 10
```

Expected output:

```text
true
```
hints: Two separate comparisons have to hold at the same time.
Join the two comparisons with your language's logical and operator.

python.solution:
def within_range(x: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> bool:
    return lo <= x <= hi


x, lo, hi = map(int, input().split())
print("true" if within_range(x, lo, hi) else "false")
